newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-SRI LANKA FACE HUGE TASK TO SAVE TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA FACE HUGE TASK TO SAVE TEST.

text.p: Sri Lanka made a better start in their second innings but still ended the third day of the first test on Sunday 327 runs in arrears against New Zealand after being forced to follow on.
Sri Lanka were 37 without loss in their second innings when rain stopped play and the umpires abandoned the day with 29 scheduled overs remaining.
Sri Lanka had earlier been dismissed for 222 in their first innings, 364 short of New Zealand's mammoth 586 for seven declared.
The tourists resumed on 78 for four in the morning, but continued to lose wickets at regular intervals as New Zealand's faster bowlers, Simon Doull and Heath Davis, dominated.
Doull finished with five for 58, while Davis captured test-best figures of three for 34 in his third test.
Hashan Tillekaratne top-scored for Sri Lanka with an unbeaten 55 and his team-mates on Monday will have to exhibit the patience which was a feature of Tillekaratne's innings.
Sri Lanka started their second innings after the tea break but were forced from the ground after nine overs because of poor light. Torrential rain then struck the ground to rule out any more play.
